item.title: Trump touts imminent decision on potential new attack on Iran
item.description: President Trump says he will make a decision "very soon" on whether to "destroy what is left of" Iran, calls Qatari emir as mediators push for a peace deal.

item.title: Employers added 165,000 jobs in October, soaring past expectations
item.description: Hiring across the U.S. surged last month and unemployment dipped, a sign the job market is picking up speed.

item.title: Is travel insurance worth it for holiday travel in 2026?
item.description: Holiday trips can come with high financial stakes. Here's when travel insurance may or may not make sense.

item.title: Musk says Tesla will end Cybertruck production next year
item.description: Tesla CEO Elon Musk said the electric car maker will halt production of its Cybertruck next year and prioritize self-driving taxis.

item.title: Doomsday cult leader learns fate for murders of 190 children
item.description: Paul Mackenzie was convicted of murdering 190 children and one adult after he ordered his followers to starve themselves to death in order to meet Jesus.

item.title: Judge blocks construction on Trump's 250-foot arch for now
item.description: The National Capital Planning Commission voted Thursday to approve plans for President Trump's 250-foot triumphal arch. A judge quickly blocked any construction from starting.

item.title: Case pitting "ER" against "The Pitt" can proceed, appeals court says
item.description: A California appeals court has found that "ER" and "The Pitt" have enough similarity that a lawsuit brought by the widow and estate of "ER" creator Michael Crichton alleging "The Pitt" is an unauthorized reboot can move forward.

item.title: Mississippi Senate race still a toss-up, with razor-thin margin
item.description: The Senate race in deep-red Mississippi remains unresolved, as Democrat Scott Colom has mounted a surprisingly competitive challenge to incumbent Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith.

item.title: 3 charged with using AI to steal some $129 million from companies
item.description: Three people accused of using artificial intelligence to impersonate corporate executives and attorneys to steal about $129 million have been indicted, prosecutors say.

item.title: Grim details emerge after woman and daughter killed by bear
item.description: The delay in finding the remains of the two women was complicated by difficult terrain and the grizzly bear's behavior.

item.title: Newly empowered Democrats could revive plans for court reforms
item.description: Democrats have proposed a variety of measures aimed at reshaping the Supreme Court over the years and may be poised to push them forward after winning House and Senate majorities.

item.title: Oil prices rebound slightly as Iran claims new attacks on ships
item.description: Oil rebounds slightly as ships continue coming under attack in the Persian Gulf after prices plunged following President Trump's midterm elections rebuke.

item.title: Midterm wave sets a course for "Medicare for All" fight
item.description: Voter frustration with healthcare costs helped fuel the Democrats' midterm takeover of Congress. But Democratic control doesn't mean "Medicare for All" will follow, as some hoped.

item.title: Stocks crater as midterms spur investor exodus from tech and AI
item.description: The tech-heavy Nasdaq is now in a "correction" as Wall Street weighs the impact of the Democrats' wins on the critical AI sector.

item.title: U.S. gas prices on track to fall below $4 a gallon, experts say
item.description: Fuel prices have dropped in recent weeks amid hopes that the midterm elections would increase pressure on the U.S. and Iran to reach a peace deal.

item.title: Newsom moves to commute all California death sentences
item.description: The move does not repeal California's death penalty or prevent prosecutors from seeking it in future cases.

item.title: Democrats flip more seats in Congress as GOP grapples with stunning losses
item.description: After Democrats' sweeping House and Senate victories, the party is laying out how it plans to wield power, while President Trump and Republicans react to their midterm losses.

item.title: Trump signs proclamation declaring Oval Office a national monument
item.description: The action does not prevent future presidents from restyling the iconic office that President Trump has filled to the brim with gold flourishes, nor does it prevent a successor from rolling back the proclamation itself.

item.title: FEMA backlog causes delays in California infrastructure projects
item.description: FEMA is behind on approving major projects to protect Southern California from floods, earthquakes, fires and landslides.

item.title: Watch: Dangerous flooding hits Georgia, Tennessee
item.description: Torrential rain hammered Georgia and Tennessee overnight, triggering catastrophic flooding in certain areas. Videos show the floods, damage and rescue efforts.

item.title: Nithya Raman ousts incumbent Karen Bass in LA mayor's race, CBS News projects
item.description: Raman's win comes after resounding victories for Democrats across the country on Election Day.

item.title: Wendy's rejects $1.4 billion hostile takeover bid
item.description: Wendy's rebuffs unsolicited offer from Trian Partners, led by activist investor Nelson Peltz, and another group of investment firms.

item.title: Democrats have flipped over 40 House seats. Here's the breakdown.
item.description: Democrats won control of the House on Tuesday by flipping more than three dozen Republican-held seats, picking up perennial swing districts and seats that were once considered deep red.

item.title: Reboots of Girls & Harry Potter: Has Hollywood Run Out of Ideas? | Straight Up with Kelly and Vlad
item.description:
Scrubs is back. Malcolm in the Middle is back. Girls, Glee and Clueless are on the way, and Harry Potter starts all over again on Christmas Day. Has Hollywood run out of ideas, or just run out of nerve?
Vlad and Kelly are breaking down reboots vs. revivals vs. spinoffs, the corporate strategy of nostalgia, and… maybe even making a plea to every show runner: don't ruin our endings.
Plus a game of Reboot or Cancel, and this week's cocktail—Déjà Brew Espresso Martinis—sponsored by Ketel One and Mr. Black.

item.title: Voters pass 44 ballot measures to restrict data centers on Election Day
item.description: Voters passed 44 measures to restrict data centers on Election Day amid concerns over their power usage and potential job losses tied to artificial intelligence. CBS News' Megan Cerullo has more.

item.title: Dolly Parton's estate moves to dismiss lawsuit against nephew
item.description: The details of the resolution between Dolly Parton's estate and her nephew, Bryan Seaver, were not immediately known.

item.title: Trump agenda likely to be curbed with Democrats in charge
item.description: Investigations, a struggle to confirm nominees and maybe some bipartisanship lie ahead for President Trump.

item.title: 11/5: CBS Evening News
item.description: Police say a gunman targeted bank employees over credit card debt; catastrophic flooding triggers evacuations and rescue efforts.

item.title: Why did Republicans lose the midterms?
item.description: Widespread Republican losses in the midterm elections are roiling the GOP, prompting soul-searching over what went wrong, and a brewing blame-game that's expected to heat up as the party looks toward the next election.

item.title: Democrats' election rout is poised to reorder health policy
item.description: Democrats' retaking of Congress doesn't change President Trump's control of the veto pen — making the new majority's aspirations to reverse changes to Medicaid, the Affordable Care Act, and other safety net programs an uphill climb.
